data.rationale: The commit fixes a parser failure in parseCheckAggregates when a whole-row Var representing a join is nulled (on the nullable side of an outer join) and referenced in a query with aggregates or a GROUP BY clause. This occurred because the parser cannot safely push down nulling bits into a RowExpr (the result of expanding a whole-row join Var) when no PlannerInfo is available. To exercise this, we need a nested join that is aliased and then placed on the nullable side of an outer join, with the join alias itself used as an expression. The grammar fragment adds a specific 'joined' alternative that creates this nested aliased structure and provides expressions to reference it in aggregation and HAVING contexts.
seeds: SELECT a1.c0, count(j_alias) FROM t1 AS a1 LEFT JOIN (t2 AS a2 JOIN t3 AS a3 ON a2.c0 = a3.c0) AS j_alias ON TRUE GROUP BY a1.c0;
SELECT j_alias, count(*) FROM t1 AS a1 LEFT JOIN (t2 AS a2 JOIN t3 AS a3 ON a2.c1 = a3.c1) AS j_alias ON TRUE GROUP BY j_alias;
SELECT 1 FROM t1 AS a1 LEFT JOIN (t2 AS a2 JOIN t3 AS a3 ON a2.c1 = a3.c1) AS j_alias ON TRUE HAVING j_alias IS NOT NULL;
